idiom_name: Askama templates compiled at build time ({% extends %}/{% block %}/{% include %})
implementation_notes: Askama compiles Jinja-style templates into Rust code at build time: a page is a struct deriving Template whose fields are the fragment's context, the layout is provided by {% extends "base.html" %} plus {% block %} ({{ super() }} chains to the parent block), and {% include "partials/row.html" %} inserts a fragment that shares the surrounding context, including loop variables. Because the template is code, a missing fragment, renamed field or type mismatch is a compile error and rendering allocates only the output; a runtime engine (Tera) is the alternative when templates must be dynamic.
pitfalls: Include and extends paths must be literal strings known at compile time - dynamic fragment selection is impossible by design, so choose a runtime engine if pages are data-driven.
Every template edit re-runs the derive and rebuilds the crate, so markup changes cost build time (and CI caches must key on templates).
Escaping is applied per file extension by the configured escaper; Askama's safe/markup filters defeat it if applied to user data.

variants.name: Tera runtime template engine
variants.idiom_name: Tera template store with {% extends %}/{% block %}/{% include %} at runtime
variants.implementation_notes: Tera is the runtime alternative: templates live as files or strings, {% extends "base.html" %} with {% block %} provides the layout, {% include "partials/row.html" %} the fragment, and Tera::new("templates/**/*.html") loads them into a store that parses once and renders per request with a typed Context. It trades compile-time checking for dynamic template loading - templates can be shipped, reloaded or selected from data - at the cost of runtime errors for missing files or wrong context keys; build the store once and clone/share it.
pitfalls: Tera::new compiles every matched template at startup: one syntax error in any file fails the whole store, so render a warmup template at boot to fail fast.
Template names and include paths must be static strings; a dynamic include path built from input is a path-traversal risk.
Building Tera per request is expensive - keep one instance in shared state (OnceLock/lazy static) and clone the cheap handle instead.
